issue #20: drops the day-before-each-change-day from the walk. add() dedupes, so this is exactly 'the predecessor is never walked'. The consequence walk then checks only minutes that cannot fail for Havana and right/America/Santiago, and the per-zone ambiguity guard must report that rather than pass.

meta-guard, not killable as a single mutant: with the day list correct no candidate is ever vacuous, so neutering the assertion changes nothing observable. Its load-bearingness is proven by the PAIR, and that was checked by hand rather than assumed: applying W15 alone the suite FAILS, applying W15 and W16 together the suite PASSES -- which is precisely the state #20 was filed from, a live bug reported green. So W15 being caught is the guard's proof, and this entry exists so nobody 'cleans up' the guard as dead code.

future-data guard: no canonical zone frees a minute on the current database, so neutering the assertion cannot fail here. It is kept because its whole job is to fire the day a tzdata edit brings the shape into canonical data, which is the same reason the property is asserted at all.

future-data guard: the measured worst canonical cost is exactly 1h, so widening the ceiling cannot fail on current data. Kept so a database that moves a canonical clock further forces the schedule.go cost sentence to be re-measured.
let changedDaysIn leak Jan 1 of the next year into this year's list, double-counting a New Year offset change in the cost figures
a declared all-day rule is reported as unreadable because its clock ends are empty
an all-day rule whose leftover times are equal is dropped as a zero-length window, enforcing nothing while the parent reads 'all day'
the flag is ignored by the evaluator: a rule with readable times enforces those times and never the whole day
a rule the parent declared is reported as a degraded reading, which trains them to ignore the report
the inferred widening stops being reported, so a rule whose clock could not be read goes quiet
